title: Senior / Staff Systems Engineer, AI Validation
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ ABOUT OUR ENGINEERING TEAMS

Wayve’s engineering teams are building the AI, robotics, simulation, data, and systems foundations needed to deploy a generalisable AI Driver safely and at scale.

ABOUT AI VALIDATION

AI Validation is a small, fast-growing team responsible for proving that the Wayve AI Driver behaves safely and effectively. The team owns end-to-end, simulation-led validation across driving competencies such as intersections, crossings, and lane changes.

🧠 YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

- Own validation for one or more driving-behaviour competencies from strategy through execution.

- Develop metrics and automated tests that connect product requirements to measurable driving performance.

- Run simulation-based evaluations, analyse results, and investigate failure modes.

- Define coverage requirements, test suites, and acceptance criteria with Product, Safety, and AV Engineering.

- Report clear findings to Release and Autonomy Engineering stakeholders.

- Work across data, simulation, and evaluation teams to remove dependencies and scale automated validation.

🧩 WHAT YOU’LL BE WORKING ON

- General-purpose metrics for on-road and simulated driving behaviour.

- Automated test frameworks for end-to-end learned driving systems.

- Scenario coverage for complex behaviour areas, including unprotected intersections, crosswalks, and lane changes.

- Validation strategies that work across multiple autonomy products.

- Evidence that directly influences release decisions and helps bring the Wayve AI Driver to customers globally.

🙌 YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

- You have hands-on experience with behaviour validation in autonomous driving, robotics, or a related product domain.

- You have worked beyond basic lane-keeping or conventional ADAS and understand L2+, L3, or L4 validation challenges.

- You can write Python professionally and have implemented metrics, tests, or evaluation tooling yourself.

- You are a systems thinker who enjoys turning ambiguous requirements into practical, automated tests.

- You can adapt to evolving simulation paradigms and communicate findings clearly.

- Experience with SQL, large datasets, AI tooling, or agentic workflows is helpful.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

MORE ABOUT WAYVE

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end-to-end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real-world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand-coded rules or pre-mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware-agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2+ through to L4 as our core AI model scales.

HOW WE WORK 💻 - LOCATIONS & FLEXIBLE WORKING

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

The successful candidate will have prior transaction monitoring/investigations experience in the financial services, FinTech or cryptocurrency industries. •
Analyze data to identify process gaps and opportunities, and partner with Compliance, Training and other FIU stakeholders to recommend mitigating activities for risk and close process gaps.

•
Evaluate AML transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting requirements for all countries where applicable.

•
Collaborate with external partners, including financial institutions, government agencies, and blockchain companies, to share intelligence and insights. Work closely with law enforcement agencies, regulators, and legal teams to provide insights and evidence for criminal investigations.

•
Stay abreast of changes to the cryptocurrency industry, financial crime trends, and regulatory requirements to assess impact to Transaction Monitoring.

•
Support team training and knowledge sharing, fostering a collaborative environment focused on ongoing learning and professional growth.

What We Look For In You 

•
3-5 years of direct and strong technical experience in BSA/AML investigations and operations in relevant financial crimes, transaction monitoring and investigation roles.

•
Demonstrated knowledge of BSA/AML, KYC regulations, risks and controls implementation globally.

•
Strong understanding of blockchain technology, cryptocurrency protocols, and decentralized networks.

•
Experience performing in a fast-paced environment and proven ability to meet deadlines.

•

title: Quality & Compliance Manager, Computer System Validation
description:

The Quality & Compliance Manager, Computer System Validation manages the quality oversight and lifecycle validation of GxP computerized systems supporting CRO and laboratory operations. The role partners with Quality, IT, system owners, operational teams, and external providers to ensure systems are fit for intended use, maintain data integrity, and remain compliant and inspection-ready from implementation through retirement. The Manager establishes consistent, risk-based computer system assurance practices and drives continuous improvement across clinical and laboratory environments.

 

MAIN DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provide independent, risk-based Quality Assurance oversight of GxP computerized systems throughout the system lifecycle, from initial assessment and implementation through operation, periodic review, significant change, and retirement.

• Review and approve applicable validation and assurance deliverables, including system risk assessments, validation plans, requirements, traceability documentation, test evidence, deviations, validation summary reports, and release-readiness documentation. • Prepare for and support sponsor audits, regulatory inspections, and internal audits involving computerized systems. Ensure validation records are complete, accurate, readily retrievable, and inspection-ready, and coordinate responses to observations within the role’s area of responsibility.

title: Head of Simulation Engineering (Expression of Interest)
description:
Expression of Interest · Inquire First
We are meeting senior leaders for this planned function as we fundraise. This is an exploratory conversation, not an immediately funded salaried vacancy or a guaranteed start date. No cash salary is available today; any equity arrangement must be agreed separately. You are not being asked to begin work by expressing interest.
Use the Apply form below to introduce yourself and indicate your interest. We can discuss mutual fit, scope, funding, compensation, and timing before either side makes a commitment.
Remote · United States · Full time · Functional leadership
Turn simulation research into an experimental engine that can be inspected, reproduced, and improved. Lead the engineering function at the boundary between scientific methods and dependable software.
Why Subconscious

Subconscious is building the intelligence to run the economy. We start with a simulator for business decisions, using causal experiments on simulated markets to test products, pricing, messaging, and go-to-market choices before capital is committed. The long-term ambition is to help businesses discover unmet demand and build around what people actually need.
The function you will build
Own simulation implementation, experiment execution semantics, reproducibility standards, and the simulation engineering hiring plan. Partner with causal research on method design, evaluation on quality, and infrastructure on reliable operation.
This is a hands-on leadership role. Set the functional roadmap and propose staffing and spending priorities with the founding team. Hiring and budget commitments depend on approved resources; an established team or funded budget is not assumed.
Proposed first 90 days after joining
Use these as an initial agenda, refined with the founders against the product, customer needs, and resources at your start.

• Trace an experiment from configuration to output and document which inputs, model versions, random states, and artifacts are required to reproduce it.

• Establish an implementation contract for treatments, populations, execution, and result aggregation, with meaningful correctness checks.

• Profile a representative workload and improve its largest quality, throughput, or cost constraint without silently changing the experimental question.

• Build a research-to-production path with versioned interfaces, reviewable changes, and explicit failure handling.

How we will judge progress
Research ideas become reusable capabilities with explainable behavior. Track reproducibility, correctness under independently specified test cases, experiment throughput, and cost. Make changes in model behavior distinguishable from execution defects.
What you bring

• You have led research engineering, simulation, scientific computing, or ML systems work and shipped robust implementations of complex methods.

• You can reason about stochastic systems, numerical behavior, experiment design, and performance while writing and reviewing production code.

• You can lead a technical roadmap across researchers and engineers and make explicit tradeoffs between exploration and stability.

We are looking for evidence of judgment, execution, and leadership. A particular company pedigree or previous executive title is not a substitute for that evidence.
Compensation and funding
We are actively fundraising. Only equity-based compensation is currently available; no cash salary is available today. The equity grant and its terms have not been set for this role and must be agreed before joining. Any future salary, incentive plan, benefits, hiring budget, or paid start date depends on financing and written agreement. Funding and its timing are not guaranteed.
Before deciding to join, discuss the grant structure, fully diluted ownership basis, vesting, dilution, applicable exercise terms, company funding position, and working arrangement. A company valuation is not the cash value of an equity grant.

title: Principal Storage Architect
description:
About Graphcore

Graphcore is a leading innovator in artificial intelligence computing. We develop hardware, software, and data center infrastructure that provide the specialized processing and systems capabilities needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.

As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore works alongside companies developing advanced technologies. Our teams bring together AI researchers, silicon designers, hardware and software engineers, and systems architects to solve complex technical problems across the computing stack.

The Opportunity

As Principal Storage Architect, you will define the high-performance storage architecture for Graphcore's AI computing and data center infrastructures.   You will lead the design of local and distributed storage tiers that provide the throughput, availability, and predictable tail latency required for large-scale training and inference.

Working within Advanced Architecture, you will address storage requirements for saving model states, offloading key-value caches, large datasets, and high-speed data-loading pipelines.   You will combine hands-on performance engineering with Principal-level technical leadership across hardware, software, networking, systems engineering, automation, supply chain, and external technology partners.

What You Will Do

• Define the end-to-end architecture and technology roadmap for local, disaggregated, and distributed storage across Graphcore AI server and data center platforms.

• Design storage topologies that optimize PCIe lane allocation, network-domain placement, and data paths among CPUs, AI accelerators, memory, and storage systems.

• Lead the architecture of storage control-plane and data-plane solutions, evaluating commercial and open technologies against performance, resilience, manageability, and lifecycle requirements.

• Profile and tune the Linux storage stack, block layer, I/O schedulers, direct I/O paths, file systems, and drivers to improve IOPS, bandwidth, and 99.99th-percentile latency.

• Optimize storage for AI workloads, including model checkpointing, key-value cache offload, data ingestion, and direct data movement between NVMe storage and accelerator memory.

• Set the technical direction for NVMe SSD lifecycle management, including qualification, provisioning, health monitoring, firmware rollout, failure handling, and warranty-return automation across E1.S, E3.S, U.2, and U.3 devices.

• Define telemetry and alerting requirements for direct-attached and distributed storage, including endurance, wear, drive writes per day, thermals, capacity, performance, and latency anomalies.

• Provide architecture requirements and technical guidance to automation teams building frameworks that characterize storage performance, reliability, and compatibility across AI platforms.

• Lead root-cause analysis for complex storage failures and performance degradation across Linux kernels, drivers, PCIe, networks, SSD firmware, and third-party storage systems.

• Partner with storage vendors, supply chain, networking, systems engineering, and product teams to select, integrate, and deploy storage components and platforms.

• Evaluate emerging storage, interconnect, and memory-tiering technologies and translate relevant developments into platform requirements and future system designs.

What You Will Bring

• A bachelor's or equivalent experience or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, information technology, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Extensive hands-on experience in storage engineering and architecture for AI, high-performance computing, hyperscale, or large data center environments, including technical leadership at Principal, Staff, or Lead Architect scope.

• Deep knowledge of NVMe, PCIe Gen5 or Gen6 architecture, NAND flash behavior, SSD form factors, endurance, firmware, and device lifecycle management.

As a Hardware Development Engineer, you will design circuit solutions for Graphcore processor systems and validation platforms. You will turn system requirements into schematics, layout constraints, and testable hardware.

Your work will shape production systems and test boards used across development, validation, and customer enablement. You will help prove performance, margin, and reliability before designs move into volume production.

Alongside silicon, architecture, software and PCB CAD specialists, you will make design decisions grounded in evidence. You will define validation plans, run lab campaigns, debug prototypes, and interpret results with firmware and architecture teams.

This role suits someone who likes owning problems from first schematic to mass production readiness. Few roles connect board design, bring-up, validation, and production so directly.

The team and culture

Hardware Engineering builds production systems and test hardware around Graphcore processors. The team works close to silicon, architecture, firmware, software, and PCB CAD from the first requirement onwards.

Engineers own designs through definition, schematic capture, layout support, bring-up, validation, and production transfer. Work moves quickly because problems are handled close to the lab, not passed between silos.

The team makes decisions through evidence: measurements, design reviews, margin data, and open technical challenge. You will speak up, take responsibility, and help the team move with confidence.

What we're looking for

· Strong digital circuit design and validation skills, including DCDC regulators, power delivery, resets, clocks, and control interfaces.
· Experience developing processor-based systems and working with interfaces such as Ethernet, PCIe, DDR, USB, QSPI and JTAG.
· Practical lab depth in bring-up, debug, margin testing, and validation using oscilloscopes, logic analysers and signal generators.

title: Data Loss Protection Consultant (Qatar location)
description:
CAPCO POLAND 

*We are looking for candidates willing to relocate to the Middle East - Qatar for the duration of the project.

At  Capco Poland, we’re not just another consultancy - we’re the spark behind digital transformation in the financial world. As a global leader in technology and management consulting, we thrive on helping clients tackle the toughest challenges across banking, payments, capital markets, wealth, and asset management.

Our secret?

A culture that’s fast, flexible, and fiercely entrepreneurial. We move quickly, think creatively, and always put our people first.

We’re passionate about growth - both for our clients and ourselves - and that means attracting the very best talent to join us on this exciting journey.

We’re proud to be:
• Trailblazers in banking, payments, capital markets, wealth, and asset management
• Champions of an agile, nimble, and innovative work environment
• Dedicated to building a team of top-notch professionals who share our drive and vision

Protect critical data. Strengthen controls. Reduce information risk.

The Role

Capco is looking for a Data Protection & DLP Consultant to help our clients protect sensitive and critical information across complex technology environments. This is an opportunity to work on complex data protection challenges within financial services, helping clients strengthen controls, reduce data leakage risks, and meet security, governance, and regulatory requirements.

The engagement is expected to run for one year and requires relocation to the Middle East for its duration . You will collaborate with client and project teams to deliver the agreed data engineering scope and project outcomes.

What You’ll Do

• Design and implement a comprehensive, multi‑layered data protection strategy incorporating data classification, data discovery, encryption controls, and DLP technologies.

• Design, implement, and enhance Data Loss Prevention policies, controls, processes, and technical solutions across enterprise environments.

• Identify and classify sensitive data, translating business and regulatory requirements into practical rules and controls.

• Monitor and assess alerts and incidents, supporting investigation, remediation, tuning, and continuous improvement.

• Work with security, data, risk, technology, and business teams to integrate DLP controls across endpoints, networks, cloud platforms, and applications.

• Maintain documentation, reporting, and governance processes associated with data protection and DLP operations.

• Support governance, reporting, control effectiveness assessments, and the development of sustainable data protection practices.

What We’re Looking For

• Strong experience in Data Loss Prevention, information protection, data security, or related cybersecurity and data disciplines.

• Practical knowledge of DLP technologies, data classification, information protection, policy management, monitoring, and incident management.

• Experience implementing or managing DLP controls across endpoints, email, networks, cloud services, and enterprise applications.

• Strong understanding of data governance, security controls, risk management, privacy, and regulatory requirements.

• Clear communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex data protection requirements into practical outcomes.

Bonus Points For

• Experience delivering DLP or data protection initiatives within banking, financial services, or another regulated environment.

• Experience with enterprise DLP and information protection platforms.

• Knowledge of cloud security, identity and access management, data discovery, encryption, or rights management.

• Relevant cybersecurity, data, cloud, or information security certifications.

• Exposure to large-scale data security, cybersecurity, regulatory, or technology transformation programmes.

title: AI Engineer
description:
Certa (certa.ai http://certa.ai) is an AI-native third-party risk management platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle, from onboarding through continuous monitoring and offboarding. Enterprises from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups use our no-code platform to manage vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. Trusted by Honeywell, Uber, MARS, and Boeing, we've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries.

We're looking for an experienced, innovative AI Engineer to push the boundaries of LLM technology and build intelligent features for our enterprise platform. Pairing strong Python and cloud backend skills with hands-on generative AI experience (LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG, and agents), you'll design and deploy AI-driven solutions from prototype to production - helping define a new class of engineering role that blends robust system design with state-of-the-art AI.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Design & ship AI features: Lead the design, development, and deployment of generative AI and LLM-powered services - intelligent chatbots, AI-driven recommendations, workflow automation - that deliver engaging, human-centric experiences.

- Build RAG pipelines: Design, implement, and continuously optimize end-to-end RAG pipelines (data ingestion and parsing, chunking, vector indexing, prompt engineering) so our systems retrieve and use knowledge accurately.

- Build LLM agents: Develop and refine LLM-based agentic systems for complex, multi-step tasks - incorporating planning, memory, and tool use, and applying emerging best practices to make agents more reliable.

- Evaluate & iterate: Rigorously evaluate models and pipelines on accuracy, latency, and hallucination rate, using thorough testing and user feedback to improve prompts, parameters, and data processing.

- Engineer for production: Write clean, maintainable, testable code with strong monitoring and logging, ensuring AI components are scalable and fit the overall system architecture.

- Collaborate & innovate: Partner with product, design, and engineering to integrate AI seamlessly into products, mentor teammates on generative AI best practices, and continuously explore new AI advancements to bring into the platform.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Software engineering: 3+ years (mid-level) / 5+ years (senior) of backend engineering, with expert Python, scalable API/service design, strong system design, and experience deploying on AWS or similar cloud platforms.

- LLM application experience: Proven experience building real products on LLMs/generative AI (chatbots, semantic search, AI assistants), with hands-on RAG and agent work and a solid grasp of model behavior and failure modes.

- Applied AI depth: Strong in prompt design, function calling/structured outputs, tool use, context-window management, and the RAG levers that matter (parsing/chunking, metadata, re-ranking, embedding/model selection); pragmatic model/provider trade-offs (latency, cost, context, safety); product-aligned evaluation (golden sets, prompt unit tests, offline checks, online A/Bs); and fundamentals of embeddings, tokenization, vector search, and transformers.

- Tooling: Hands-on with LLM orchestration libraries (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and vector databases (Pinecone, Chroma, Milvus).

- Cloud & DevOps: Able to productionize LLM/RAG services as high-availability, low-latency backends on AWS (ECS/EKS/Lambda, API Gateway/ALB, S3, DynamoDB/Postgres, OpenSearch, SQS/SNS/Step Functions, KMS, VPC) with IaC (Terraform/CDK), strong observability, security (PII handling, encryption, least-privilege IAM), progressive delivery (blue/green, canary, feature flags), and cost/latency strategies like caching, batching, streaming, and multi-provider fallbacks.

title: Data Scientist (BESS Performance Engineer)
description:
BESS Performance Engineer
We are:
Wizeline , a global AI-native technology solutions provider, develops cutting-edge, AI-powered digital products and platforms. We partner with clients to leverage data and AI, accelerating market entry and driving business transformation. As a global community of innovators, we foster a culture of growth, collaboration, and impact.
With the right people and the right ideas, there’s no limit to what we can achieve.
Are you a fit?
We are seeking a BESS Performance Engineer to join the Asset Management team, supporting a growing portfolio of distributed generation projects across the United States. Reporting to the VP of Engineering, this role will lead performance monitoring, analysis, and reporting for standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and solar-plus-storage assets, including AC- and DC-coupled configurations.
The ideal candidate combines expertise in battery performance modeling, renewable energy systems, and data analytics to optimize technical performance and commercial efficiency. Working closely with Data Science, Asset Management, Engineering, and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) teams, this individual will develop data-driven insights, automate reporting workflows, and identify opportunities to improve asset reliability, battery life, and energy market performance.
Key Responsibilities

•
BESS Performance Monitoring: Lead performance analysis, monitoring, and operational reporting for standalone BESS and paired solar PV + BESS assets across a distributed generation portfolio.

•
KPI Development & Tracking: Develop and monitor key performance indicators, including Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE), State of Health (SOH), State of Charge (SOC), auxiliary power consumption, and system availability.

•
Battery Degradation & Predictive Modeling: Develop degradation models and predictive analytics to forecast battery life, monitor SOH against capacity guarantees, and optimize charging and discharging cycles.

•

title: Narrative Designer
description:
About the game
Hopetown is a new narrative-first RPG inspired by Disco Elysium, being built by some of the team that worked on Disco Elysium, including Martin Luiga (founder of the ZA/UM Cultural Movement, writer of several characters on Disco Elysium, writer of the first short story in the Disco Elysium world), Lenval Brown (narrator of Disco Elysium) and Piotr Sobolewski (former CEO of Knights of U, which completed all the tech for Disco Elysium).
We are currently moving into early production, building out the foundational systems, characters, and mechanics that will define the experience. With your help, we can transform Hopetown from a great cRPG into an unforgettable one - a living, breathing universe of stories, surprises, and challenges.
About us
Longdue is a studio founded to create rich, emotional, story-first games that challenge players’ expectations. We’re a remote team of writers, artists, designers, and engineers, bringing together talent from across the industry to push the boundaries of narrative-driven RPGs.
We are still early in production, meaning new team members will have a real, tangible impact on the world we are building. We believe that extraordinary games can come from small, focused teams that value creativity, openness, and care over convention.
About the role
We’re looking for a Lead Narrative Designer with both creative and production instincts - someone who can shape Hopetown’s story while helping to build the systems and structures that make great narrative work possible.
You’ll lead a small team of writers through the early stages of development, balancing storytelling vision with clear planning, coordination, and delivery. You’ll collaborate closely with design, production, and tech to align narrative goals with development milestones and to ensure the narrative team’s output fits smoothly into the broader pipeline.
This role sits at the intersection of creativity and operations - ideal for someone who loves story but also thrives on clarity, structure, and collaboration.
Add to What You’ll Be Doing:

• We’re looking for a Narrative Lead with both creative and production instincts, someone who can shepherd Hopetown’s story while helping us refine systems and structures that make great narrative work possible.

• You’ll lead a small team of writers, balancing storytelling vision with clear planning, coordination, and delivery. You’ll collaborate closely with design, production, and tech to align narrative goals with development milestones and to ensure the narrative team’s output fits smoothly into the broader pipeline.

• This role sits at the intersection of creativity and operations, ideal for someone who loves story but also thrives on clarity, structure, and collaboration.

Requirements
MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

• 5+ years of experience leading and/or managing a narrative team on a narrative-first game, ideally in the RPG space.

• Proven ability to plan, organise, and deliver narrative work within production milestones, experience coordinating pipelines, tracking progress, and aligning with design or production teams

• Proven experience writing emotionally resonant, character-driven stories

title: ServiceNow Developer
description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place!

We are looking for a hands-on ServiceNow Developer to join our IT Platform team. This person will own the day-to-day configuration, development, and support of our ServiceNow instance, working across ITSM & HRSD while helping extend the platform through custom development and third-party integrations. This is a highly technical, delivery-focused role for someone who enjoys building, troubleshooting, and continuously improving a mission-critical enterprise platform.

You'll work across our development, staging, and production instances, partner closely with IT and business stakeholders, and help drive our upgrade and enhancement roadmap forward.

What you’ll be doing:

- Develop and configure ServiceNow: Build and maintain applications, catalog items, record producers, workflows, Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, Script Includes, UI Actions, and other platform components.

- Build integrations: Design, develop, and troubleshoot integrations between ServiceNow and third-party systems using REST/SOAP APIs, OAuth, webhooks, Integration Hub, MCP, and iPaaS platforms such as Workato.

- Maintain and optimize the platform: Monitor platform health, troubleshoot performance issues, optimize scripts and flows, and ensure solutions remain scalable and maintainable.

- Support ServiceNow applications like ITSM & HRSD: Help deliver and improve Incident, Problem, Change, Request, and HR-related workflows and automations.

- Manage access and security: Administer roles, ACLs, permissions, and other platform access controls in line with security and audit requirements.

- Resolve complex issues: Act as an escalation point for platform-level incidents, perform root cause analysis, and coordinate with infrastructure, security, vendors, and other technical teams when issues span multiple systems.

- Deliver enhancements and projects: Partner with stakeholders to gather requirements, prioritize the backlog, design solutions, and take work through development, testing, deployment, and post-launch support.

- Drive platform consistency: Establish reusable development patterns and standards for workflows, notifications, approvals, documentation, and user experiences.

- Support upgrades and releases: Evaluate new ServiceNow releases, test upgrades, remediate breaking changes, and adopt relevant new platform capabilities.

- Document and enable: Maintain technical documentation, runbooks, integration documentation, and user procedures, and provide support or training when needed.

What you need to bring:

- Hands-on experience developing and administering ServiceNow, ideally across ITSM and/or HRSD.

- Strong JavaScript skills, including ServiceNow scripting APIs such as GlideRecord and GlideAjax.

- Experience with Flow Designer, Business Rules, Script Includes, Client Scripts, UI Policies, UI Actions, ACLs, and Service Catalog development.

- Experience designing and troubleshooting REST/SOAP integrations, OAuth, webhooks, and enterprise integrations.

- Strong understanding of ITSM processes and how they translate into ServiceNow solutions.

- Ability to independently troubleshoot complex issues across ServiceNow and connected systems.

- Strong problem-solving, communication, and documentation skills.

- Experience working with stakeholders to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions.

- Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to have's

- Experience with HRSD, ITOM, Workday, or identity/HR platforms.

- Experience with ServiceNow AI/GenAI capabilities, including Now Assist.

- Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and MCP-enabled tools or workflows.

- Experience with Service Portal, custom widgets, HTML, and CSS.

- Experience with Workato or other iPaaS platforms.

- ServiceNow CSA or CAD, or ITIL 4 Foundation

title: Head of Growth
description:
About LumiMeds

LumiMeds is a fast-growing U.S.-based telehealth startup focused on weight management and long-term metabolic health. We are building the next generation of e-commerce and clinical infrastructure from the ground up.

As an early-stage company, we move quickly, operate with limited layers, and expect high ownership from every team member. There is no bureaucracy here - decisions happen fast, priorities evolve, and builders thrive.

We are a remote-first, globally distributed team that values clarity, accountability, and people who take initiative rather than wait for direction.

Head of Growth - LumiMeds

Location: Remote | Type: Full-time | Reports to: Founder/CEO

About LumiMeds

LumiMeds is a fast-growing telehealth company making GLP-1 weight-loss treatment (semaglutide & tirzepatide) accessible, affordable, and effective. We've built a real business with real patients and real outcomes - and we're just getting started. We move fast, test relentlessly, and let data settle arguments.

The Role

We're hiring a Head of Growth to own our growth engine end-to-end - online and offline. This is not a channel-manager seat. You'll set the growth strategy, run experiments across every lever (paid, organic, referral, partnerships, experiential, OOH, guerrilla), and personally drive the initiatives that move the business. You bring a playbook of proven tactics, the scrappiness to execute them on a lean budget, and the analytical rigor to know what's actually working.

If you've grown a consumer business from scratch, thrive in ambiguity, and get a thrill out of finding the unlock nobody else saw - this is your seat.

What You'll Do

•
Own the full growth strategy across digital and offline channels - you set the roadmap and the number you're accountable to.

•
Run growth end-to-end: ideation → hypothesis → execution → measurement → iterate. You don't hand things off; you drive them to the finish.

•
Build and scale offline growth initiatives - experiential, OOH, guerrilla, events, partnerships, retail, and channels we haven't thought of yet.

•
Scale digital acquisition - paid social/search, lifecycle, referral, affiliate, SEO/content - and squeeze efficiency out of every dollar.

•
Bring proven playbooks - you've done this before and can point to specific tactics that worked, and why.

•
Research relentlessly - find new channels, size opportunities, study competitors, and pressure-test ideas before we spend.

•
Negotiate with vendors and partners - you get more for less and structure deals that de-risk our spend.

•
Live in the data - instrument everything, measure CAC/LTV/payback obsessively, and kill what doesn't work fast.

What You Bring

•
Track record of growing a business - you can show real numbers you were directly responsible for moving.

•
Both offline and digital growth experience - you're equally comfortable running a guerrilla campaign and a paid-acquisition dashboard.

•
A documented playbook of growth tactics you've run and can run again.

•
True growth-hacker DNA - scrappy, resourceful, and biased toward action on a lean budget.

•
Data-driven decision-making - you form hypotheses, run clean tests, and follow the numbers.

•
End-to-end ownership - you take an idea from napkin to launched, measured, and scaled.

•
Strong research and negotiation skills - you find the opportunity and close the deal.

• Bonus: DTC, subscription, telehealth, wellness, or regulated-vertical experience.

Why LumiMeds

• Direct access to the founder and a mandate to move fast.

• A real product with proven demand and outcomes - you're pouring fuel on a fire, not starting one.

• Full ownership of growth, with the budget and autonomy to prove your playbook.

How to Apply

If this role sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application in English and ensure your resume reflects relevant experience for the role.

The robots run on advanced boards that cover a wide range of electrical engineering. On one end is high power, such as battery and motor controllers. On the other end are high-speed interfaces like PCIe, USB and MIPI CSI. The real challenge is making all these subsystems work together as one system. Many of these problems have no textbook solution. Solving them takes solid experience, a deep understanding of the physics and a creative mind. The EE team is small, and the robot is far from finished. You’ll own your boards end to end : requirements, system design, schematic, layout, design review, sourcing, manufacturing, testing and validation. You’ll keep owning them for as long as they’re in prod

description:
Remote, Philippines

Looking for Builders, Not Passengers
Most engineers are given maps.
We are looking for someone who creates the roadmap .
We are building an AI company at speed. The kind where the architecture decisions made in the next 12-18 months will define our company for the next decade.
This role is not for someone who wants a comfortable sprint cycle.
It’s for someone who wants to build systems that matter, someone who is comfortable assembling parts of an airplane while the airplane is in the air.
We are looking for a Driven and Talented Software Engineer who can operate with the ownership, speed, and sound judgment of a leader.
Someone who doesn’t wait to be pointed at problems.
Someone who hunts them and solves them graciously.
The Work
You won’t be maintaining legacy systems.
You’ll be building the core systems that drive change and impact a significant number of extremely reputable and large businesses.
That means:

• Designing architecture that scales before the scale exists

• Turning ambiguous ideas into production systems quickly

• Shipping fast while protecting the parts that cannot break

• Making technical decisions with long half-lives

You will have real ownership of critical infrastructure, product, and platform decisions.
When something blocks progress, you remove the blocker .
No drama. Just velocity.

The Kind of Engineer Who Thrives Here
This role is intentionally polarizing.
You’ll probably thrive here if:

• You build things because you can’t help yourself

• You care deeply about craft, performance, and elegant systems

• You move faster than most teams while maintaining high standards

• You learn new domains faster than most people can Google them

•
You default to ownership instead of permission

You likely have at least one project where:

• you built something that was technically extremely difficult from scratch

• people now depend on it

•
and you did it mostly because you wanted to see if it was possible

You have very high standards .
For your code.
For your thinking.
And especially for yourself.

What This Is Not
This is not:

• a maintenance role

• a Jira-ticket factory

• a place to hide behind processes

• an environment tolerant of mediocre engineering

We are building with controlled velocity :
Fast without being sloppy.
Ambitious without being reckless.

The Upside
If you are the right person, this will be one of the most leveraged periods of your career.
You’ll get:

• Ownership over systems that matter

• A small team of other high-agency builders

• Real influence on product and architecture

• Equity that actually means something if we win

• A front-row seat to building an AI company’s new products from the ground up

The Filter
This role is not for everyone.
Most engineers prefer clear maps and tickets, predictable scope, and stable systems.
If reading this made you feel slightly uncomfortable and excited at the same time , you are probably the kind of builder we are looking for.

title: Fan Page Manager — Run Monster Run
description:
About the Role

Run Monster Run is looking for a creative social media enthusiast to help grow our presence on TikTok and Instagram and build a community of people who genuinely love our content.

Your mission? Turn our existing animation into scroll-stopping clips, hilarious moments, and content people want to share with their friends. But it's not just about chasing views or racking up followers. We want to reach the right audience: people who connect with our characters, get invested in our stories, and want to engage with the world of Run Monster Run.

We're looking for someone who knows their way around social media, can spot a viral moment from a mile away, and understands what makes people stop scrolling, hit share, leave a comment, and come back for more.

You don't need to be a professional video editor with years of experience. We care more about your creativity, social media instincts, understanding of online fandoms, and ability to create content that gets people genuinely excited about what they're watching.

What You'll Do

• Run and grow Run Monster Run's TikTok and Instagram fan pages, keeping the content fresh, engaging, and consistent.

• Hunt for the funniest, wildest, most surprising, or most memorable moments in our animated episodes and turn them into short-form videos people want to share.

• Edit and repurpose existing content into clips that capture attention and introduce new audiences to Run Monster Run.

• Find creative ways to connect with fans, spark conversations, and encourage people to engage with our characters and stories.

• Stay on top of social media trends, viral formats, and fandom culture to spot opportunities that make sense for our audience.

• Experiment with hooks, captions, editing styles, and formats to discover what resonates with viewers.

• Keep an eye on performance, looking beyond views and follower counts to understand what drives meaningful engagement, shares, comments, and repeat interactions.

• Build a consistent posting rhythm while making sure every piece of content feels relevant to the Run Monster Run audience and the world of the show.

What We're Looking For

• Hands-on experience managing TikTok and/or Instagram accounts, ideally with a track record of growing an audience and generating strong engagement.

• A portfolio of short-form edits, clips, Reels, or other social-media-first content that demonstrates your creativity and ability to capture attention.

• Strong instincts for identifying compelling moments and turning them into content that makes people laugh, react, comment, or share.

• A solid understanding of internet culture, viral trends, and online fandoms, including what makes people connect with a show, its characters, and its stories.

• An audience-first mindset: you understand that building a successful account is about more than follower counts. You care about attracting people who genuinely connect with the content and want to engage with it.

• Experience growing fan pages, entertainment accounts, or social media accounts built around existing shows, characters, celebrities, or other IPs.

• A genuine interest in animation and animated shows, with an appreciation for the communities and fandoms that grow around them.

• A creative, proactive approach to testing ideas, learning from results, and finding new ways to grow an engaged audience.
